question: What was Apple's effective tax rate, and why was it below the US statutory rate?

answer.summary: Apple's effective tax rate for FY2023 was 14.7%, down 150 bps from 16.2% in FY2022 and up from 13.3% in FY2021 [F00608][F00609][F00610]. The rate was below the US federal statutory rate primarily because of a lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings, the US federal R&D credit, and tax benefits from share-based compensation, partially offset by state income taxes [T00347]. The FY2023 decline versus FY2022 was driven mainly by a lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings and the impact of US foreign tax credit regulations issued by the Treasury in 2022, partially offset by lower tax benefits from share-based compensation [T00348]. Income tax expense was $16.74B on pre-tax income of $113.74B in FY2023 [F00046][F00043]. The statutory federal rate itself is referenced in the filing's rate-reconciliation table but its numeric value is not in the retrieved evidence [T00345]. Gross unrecognized tax benefits were $19.5B as of September 30, 2023, of which $9.5B would impact the effective rate if recognized [T00527].
drivers: Below-statutory rate in FY2023: lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings, US federal R&D credit, and tax benefits from share-based compensation, partially offset by state income taxes [T00347]

FY2023 vs FY2022 decline of 150 bps: lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings and impact of 2022 US foreign tax credit regulations, partially offset by lower tax benefits from share-based compensation [T00348][F00608]
risks_and_red_flags: Gross unrecognized tax benefits rose to $19.5B (from $16.8B a year earlier), with $9.5B (vs $8.0B) that would impact the effective tax rate if recognized — a potential future rate volatility source [T00527]
Reliance on foreign-earnings mix and R&D credits means the rate is sensitive to changes in foreign tax regulations and credit eligibility [T00347][T00348]
data_quality_notes: The unrecognized-tax-benefit figures in [T00527] are marked unchecked against the tables; verify against the income tax footnote before use
The numeric statutory federal income tax rate is referenced in the rate-reconciliation table but is not present in the retrieved evidence [T00345]
The two derived series show a 1 bp rounding difference for the FY2023 change (-150 bps [F00608] vs -149 bps [F01407]); both round to a ~1.5 pp decline

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 effective tax rate of 14.7% on $113.74B pre-tax income, producing $16.74B of tax expense; the rate fell 150 bps from FY2022's 16.2% [F00608][F00046][F00043]
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: No forward-looking tax-rate guidance is in the retrieved evidence
